claims.name: The Career Academies evaluation randomly assigned applicants in nine high schools and followed outcomes for eight years after scheduled graduation.
Career Academy group members earned an average 11% more per year than controls over the eight-year follow-up ($2,088 in 2006 dollars).
Career Academies did not show an overall advantage in postsecondary educational attainment over eight years.
Career Academy earnings gains were concentrated among young men: $3,731 per year (17%) over the eight-year follow-up.
